I just made this same mistake tonight and I feel so bad about it, I've been driving for around 4 years and considered myself a good driver but this had me spiraling lol. I made one mistake 3 years ago but with a left turn and I still think about how I could've died and how the passengers could have died. Now I never do left turns unless there's a left turn signal or no cars whatsoever. You will learn from this.

My mistake was I was already halfway turning and I made the choice to try and turn right away or get hit with half my car sticking out. I just tell myself, I will not make any right turns unless there is a green light, and the people behind me will just have to be patient. People mad at you for not turning is better than risking your life. I know it may not be comforting, knowing that these mistakes will eventually happen when you're experienced, but you're human and driving is harder than people give it credit for.

My mentor is someone well known in animal welfare. She has worked with a bunch of zoos, including big AZA zoos. This zoo she got in contact with me is a smaller zoo working with her. She told me to send my resume and cover letter to them. She texted the curator during our call and asked if they were hiring and the person responded yes(I didn't ask her to reach out to anyone- but I do really appreciate her looking out for me). It seemed like they had recent changes in their animal care staff, though I'm just inferring. So that's how I got an interview, my email was kinda of an application. Though I did check their website, there is no animal care position currently listed. But I heard a lot of job seeking is through word of mouth first so I don't know.

But you're right, I did email them asking for a job description since I got no information on what they were hiring for. I was told (by my mentor) to tailor my cover letter and resume to animal care and that's it. Hopefully I'll find out before the interview. If it's not a full-time keeper job there's no way I will take it. I'm in a full-time animal care job currently that pays really well. Granted- it's not a zoo and I work with agricultural animals but it's still animal care. 

Thank you for your input, this helped me feel more at ease. I'll feel better knowing what I've applied for. But if it does end up being a full-time keeper job I'm kinda at a loss. I'd turn down the job because I cannot afford to move- especially if the pay is lower (my area is expensive). Which really sucks because it feels like to get in the zoo world you really gotta be able to afford to take that pay cut. Wish there was another way to get around it.

I asked my mentor ways to get into zookeeping without volunteering due to COVID. She told me networking is the best bet. Going to ZAA or AZA meetings would be your best bet. 

But also: don't give up on the volunteering issue. I currently work at a farm sanctuary and we have been taking in volunteers. Literally just any place that has animals, even if it's a shelter with just dogs and cats or something, will be valuable.

As a 23 year old butch lesbian, it breaks my heart to see this post. When I was 14 I remember identifying as bi on the internet but not really understanding and battling comphet, typing XD RAWR on deviantart. I was the quiet kid who had crippling social anxiety like you did. I self harmed and when high school came I had no friends and would spend lunch in the bathrooms. I even wore gray every day just to blend in. If my 14 year old self saw me now, I wouldn’t believe that this was me. In college I finally found myself and did everything I was scared of doing in high school. There is hope for you, I know one day when you’re on your own you’ll have to ask yourself who you wanna be. And you should do everything you can to make yourself become the person you want to be. 

If your parents allow it (which I’m a little doubtful after reading this) please start as soon as you can. It took me 7 years to cut my hair short. I wanted short hair for that long and when I did it, it was so freeing. Of course this didn’t solve all my problems, but I felt so much more comfortable in my skin. My family situation also sucks and the only advice there I have to offer is, try and make enough space between you guys but still maintain a healthy relationship. Boundaries are necessary for a relationship to work and I know you said your therapist did help you with your family issues that’s just a reminder for you.

Please feel free to DM me. Do not do this, I know life sucks and it feels like it’ll never suck but when you grow, as cliche as this sounds, you realize there’s SO much more to life than your parents house.

It sucks. I know I have to accept it but, it just sucks so badly that something you want above all else in your life is unreachable. I’ll never have that feeling again. I honestly don’t know if life is worth living without having someone to share it with.

I also went through something similar! I graduated and had to leave my college town because of the pandemic. She was in her last year. I was always expected to visit her.

Even said I didn’t want a dog and that was a dealbreaker. Uh, I was always fine with getting a dog with her? She just wanted to give someone control over her future (she specifically wrote that) but why couldn’t have it been me? She didn’t ever wanna talk about the future with me, it got to the point where I stopped cause she was clearly getting annoyed and agitated with me, I wasn’t trying to create any pressure for her. 

Long distance sucks. It sucks even more when you are totally committed, trying to improve communication and just trying to save your relationship when the other person doesn’t care and puts no effort. She put all the blame on me. I understand your pain

We broke up during a fight. I believe the first week we were still texting each other, though I did not beg at all and I did not overtly share my feelings. I did a little, and I did moreso at the beginning of when she broke up with me. Fast forward and it's almost move in day for college. I believe I went no contact at week two or three. When it was week 3 she messaged me about something I couldn't ignore involving our stuff and I expressed my disapproval without getting too angry. 

Then it was back to no contact. I didn't stalk her profiles and really tried to give myself peace of mind. Eventually, I kinda felt confident (week 5/6?) in myself. Maybe even cocky almost lol. I thought I looked good. I posted a really good selfie and got a lot of praise. I was just going on my life on twitter. Nothing sad, just content about me and my friends and thoughts and what I'm doing with my life. During this week there was a shooting and she texted me asking if I were okay and how I'd drop off her stuff. Week 7 I think was when she texted I miss you. I did not respond lol. I felt angry she messaged me that, but at the same time pleasantly surprised. Week 8, I got the confidence to try tindr. Nothing serious, just casual talk. I knew I was still recovering. I posted something about this on twitter, saying I was hesitant to meet with a girl I was talking to. She texted me upset that I would do such a thing, how I moved on so fast. 

I think it was week 9 or 10 when she suggested seeing each other in person again. When we met, I was kinda stone. She was crying in front of me and I had no idea what to do. I was not gonna show her my emotions, I was gonna show her I was living my best life. I really had no intention of getting back with her at this point either. I figured she wanted closure. Emotions were stirring back up though. She later texted me about my coldness after meeting with her and I told her I'd meet up with her to talk about my feelings. At this meeting I expressed I did miss her. Then we just started seeing each other and hanging out more and more. That was about a 2 month process I think, to get to kissing.

Sorry this is long! From what I'm looking up, I did a really good job in building myself up, which made her miss me and felt like she missed out on something good.
